solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like total energy? Take it!

parts.note: 'as' means in the same way as, like
a total is a sum
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A physics question about total energy, followed by an invitation to take something for granted.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and exclamation mark split the clue: the wordplay comes first and 'Take it!' is an instruction meaning take it as given.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something as true without proof is to presume it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: At sea, Pan broke foot

indicators.note: the letters of at sea and pan are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Out at sea, the god Pan broke his foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' is a metrical unit of verse, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody, this is a metrical foot of two short syllables followed by a long one.

clue.text: Some sharks possibly near to eating ordinary student

parts.note: a school is a group of fish, sharks perhaps

indicators.note: the word for near eats the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: by means near, as in stand by

explanation.surface: Sharks circling close to devouring an ordinary student.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy who attends school is a young pupil, so he is a student.

clue.text: See 26
Sail away when detective goes round capital city

indicators.note: the detective's letters go round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector in British police ranks
a jib is a triangular sail at a boat's bow
out means away, not at home

explanation.surface: A sailor departs while a police detective circles the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sail' and 'away' are separate pieces, not the phrase 'jib out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Djibouti is the capital of the Horn of Africa republic of the same name.

clue.text: Bench-sitter merely rocks

parts.note: just means merely, only
rocks is slang for ice, as in a drink on the rocks

explanation.surface: Someone sitting on a bench who simply rocks back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bench' is the judiciary; 'Bench-sitter' looks like a park loiterer.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge, who sits on the bench in court, is formally addressed by this title.

clue.text: Book containing directions to act rationally

indicators.note: the book contains the directions, which sit inside it

parts.note: the Bible is the Book
E, S, E, N, S are compass directions east, south, east, north, south

explanation.surface: A manual containing directions for acting sensibly.
explanation.definitionFit: To act sensibly or use good judgement is to behave reasonably and with sound reasoning.

clue.text: Plant rust in pasture doubles

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words pasture doubles, across the word boundary

explanation.surface: Plant rust in a meadow multiplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Uredo is a stage of rust fungi that attacks plants, a botanical term for the disease.

clue.text: Actually dropping around for new baby

indicators.note: the letter meaning around is dropped from the phrase
something is put in place of the dropped letter, here the letter for new

parts.note: in fact means actually
C stands for circa, around

explanation.surface: Actually giving up the old for a brand new baby.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child, a babe in arms.

clue.text: Greedy-guts princess seen in sports car

indicators.note: the princess is seen in the car, placed inside it

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a sports car
Anne is the British Princess Royal

explanation.surface: A greedy royal spotted in a sports car.
explanation.definitionFit: A gannet is British slang for a glutton, from the seabird's voracious appetite.

clue.text: Contents of mail described answer for city-dwellers

wordplay.reading: mail's inside is A, then I; answer is ANS

parts.note: the inside letters of mail, described in words, are 'A then I', and answer is abbreviated ANS

explanation.surface: Someone describes the contents of the post as the answer for people in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Rather than taking the middle letters directly, the clue describes them: the middle of 'mail' is A, then I, and the word THEN is spelt out in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of the Greek capital Athens are its inhabitants, so they are urban residents.

clue.text: Will novelist take hours to find place to store books?

indicators.note: the novelist takes the hours letter into his name, holding it inside

parts.note: Will Self is an English novelist

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a writer will need hours to find space for books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the future tense but is the first name of the novelist Will Self.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf is a horizontal board where volumes are kept, so it is a storage spot for reading matter.

clue.text: Supported by Q's predecessors

parts.note: the letters that come before Q in the alphabet, read as a span from the first letter to the one just ahead of Q, give a word for resting on top of something

explanation.surface: Something held up by whatever came before Q, perhaps a spymaster in Bond films.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters preceding Q are A to P, written as a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on top of another thing rests on it and is held up by it, so the preposition fits.

clue.text: American cereal is old Bollywood joke

parts.note: Bollywood is the Indian film industry, so it stands for Indian
corn is trite, hackneyed humour, the kind of old joke heard too often

explanation.surface: Remarking that a film-industry gag is as old as a breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize, the grain native to the Americas, is also known by this name.

clue.text: Many online somehow not living up to their description

definitions.text: not living up to their description

indicators.note: the letters of many online are somehow reorganised

explanation.surface: Many people online somehow fail to match their profiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nominal exists in title alone, without the substance the label suggests.

clue.text: Smaller piece of cake in clubs?

indicators.note: the cake goes in, placed inside the card suit

parts.note: clubs is one suit in a pack of cards
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: Asking whether a smaller slice of cake is served in golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests golf or societies; here it is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A component forming part of a larger unit is a subordinate section of it.

clue.text: Show pairs of events, including ceilidhs

indicators.note: the opening two letters of each of the three following words are taken

explanation.surface: A show putting together pairs of events, ceilidhs among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pairs of' applies to all three words, including 'including', which looks like a link word: EV, IN and CE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a quality is to display or reveal it, a verb synonym of show.

clue.text: Nearly cool down criminal minority

indicators.note: nearly the whole word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: to chill is to cool
D marks a down clue in crossword references
a hood is a hoodlum, a criminal

explanation.surface: Almost calming down a criminal minority group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minority' means the state of being a minor, not a small group. With 21 down it forms the last of the seven ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Minority in the legal sense is the period of being underage, the years before adulthood.

clue.text: Captive rips off a Republican

indicators.note: off means awry, so the letters of rips are rearranged

parts.note: one means a, a single

explanation.surface: A captive tears into a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive is someone held in confinement, a synonym for a jailed person.

clue.text: Cheat a lot, coming back in for generator

indicators.note: the reversed lot goes in the cheat word

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them

indicators.note: the word for a lot comes back, read from right to left

parts.note: many means a lot

explanation.surface: A swindler cheats heavily and returns to sell a generator.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a machine producing electrical current, so it is an electricity generator.

clue.text: Greek myth I souped up

indicators.note: souped up means modified, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone confessing to jazzing up a Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Thebes who killed his father and wed his mother is a figure of Greek legend.

clue.text: Squaddie starts to sing raucously, covering 60s hit?

indicators.note: the two initials cover, wrapping around, the old hit
only the first letters of sing and raucously are used

parts.note: a hit record from the sixties is now an oldie

explanation.surface: An army private belts out a rowdy cover version of a sixties hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' suggests a cover version, but it means the initials go around OLDIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A squaddie is British slang for a private in the army, a rank-and-file fighting man.

clue.text: Following the leader back

definitions.meaning: coming next after the one in front, as in a race
to back a motion or proposal is to support it formally

explanation.surface: Following the leader from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: With 17 down it forms the last of the seven ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Next after the first in order, and as a verb, to support a proposal.

clue.text: See 26
Nasty dung locked out at the first opportunity

indicators.note: the letters of dung locked are given a nasty mix-up

explanation.surface: Nasty dung is locked out of the way at the first chance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter dismissed first ball without scoring is out for a golden duck.
explanation.definitionFit: This cricket term describes being dismissed by the very first ball faced, with no runs.

clue.text: Enthusiast finished Latin first

indicators.note: first places the Latin letter at the front of the word for finished

parts.note: over means finished, done

explanation.surface: An enthusiast who has finished studying Latin first.
explanation.definitionFit: A devotee of something, such as a music fan, is called a lover of it.

clue.text: Writes programs, not third-rate poems

indicators.note: the third-rate letter is not included, so it is removed

parts.note: a programmer codes, writing software
C is the grade for third-rate, after A and B

explanation.surface: A programmer who writes code, not second-rate poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, usually addressed to a subject, so they are a kind of verse.

clue.text: Gove fan seems an anomaly in Shakespearean list seen here

indicators.note: an anomaly is something irregular, so these letters appear out of order

explanation.surface: A fan of the politician Michael Gove seems out of place in a Shakespeare speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The list is Jaques' speech in 'As You Like It'; its stages (INFANT, SCHOOLBOY, LOVER, SOLDIER, JUSTICE, PANTALOON, SECOND CHILDHOOD) are answers in this grid, hence 'seen here'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaques' 'All the world's a stage' speech lists life's seven stages, which appear throughout this grid.

clue.text: Gasp at a diver becoming Italian comedy character

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath
the loon, or great northern diver, is a diving bird

explanation.surface: Gasping at a diver who turns into a character from Italian comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diver' is a bird, the loon, not a swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantalone is the foolish old man of the commedia dell'arte, anglicised under this name.

clue.text: Australian engineers' land measure

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers of the British Army

explanation.surface: An Australian engineers' unit for measuring land.
explanation.definitionFit: An are is a metric area unit of one hundred square metres.

clue.text: Middle-aged swimmer takes in oxygen pretty regularly

indicators.note: the swimmer takes the other letters into its middle

parts.note: a fish is a swimmer
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: every other letter of pretty is used, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A middle-aged swimmer gulping oxygen fairly steadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty' looks like 'quite' here but gives its alternate letters RTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Around the age of forty is a common marker of middle life.

clue.text: Number — the German kind

parts.note: ten is a number
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A number, then a German of a certain kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender-hearted person is gentle and caring, so the adjective matches kind.
